title: Paystride Visa Payroll Card Advantage: Taking Back Provisional Credit Above What a Resolved Claim Is Due
content:
For a card on the Paystride Visa Payroll Card Advantage plan, the claim reversal schedule for the Advantage plan prices the reversal on a resolved lost or stolen card claim. The reversal takes back the part of the claim's provisional credit that stands above what the claim is due once it is resolved with an error found.

## Which claim

The reversal is on the account's most recently registered claim of an unauthorized transaction that was handled under Regulation E error resolution and resolved with an error found. The schedule prices it only when that claim:
- carries a loss date;
- carries a provisional credit with no reversal of it;
- is the only claim of its loss resolved with an error found, a claim's loss being the account's unauthorized-transaction claims carrying its loss date;
- has a loss whose liability limit can be timed. The account's replacement orders placed less than 12 whole months before today must include at most one for a lost card and at most one for a stolen card, with exactly one of them placed on or after the loss date.

Orders placed 12 or more months before today never count. Under Paystride's program practice an account with repeated lost or stolen cards within those 12 months is referred to Paystride's card fraud review team, so the schedule books nothing for its claims. Otherwise the schedule prices nothing and the base rule applies. As the base rule requires, the reversal posts only after 5 business days have passed since the resolution date. Business days are Monday through Friday excluding Federal Reserve holidays, counted from the day after the earlier date through the later one.

## Effect

When no error, or a smaller error, is found, the provisional credit's excess over what the claim is due is debited back by a reversal pointing to the provisional credit. On a claim this schedule prices, and only on such a claim, what the claim is due is the amount this schedule sets out. The claim reversal schedule for the Premier and Elite plans states its own.

The excess of a provisional credit is not taken back until every final credit owed on the account's other claims of a lost or stolen card has posted.

Equivalently, no excess is taken back while the account's other lost or stolen card claims include one owed a final credit that has not posted.

## `take_back_card_claim_excess_b240170d`

| Block | Contract |
|---|---|
| Capability | Takes back, from a payroll card account on an Advantage plan, part or all of the provisional credit posted on a resolved claim about a lost or stolen card. On success, one provisional credit reversal for the stated amount is added to the account, pointing to that claim's provisional credit, and the card's available balance falls by that amount. The cardholder sees the reversal on the card history. |
| Invocation | Agent-side: the agent unlocks `take_back_card_claim_excess_b240170d` and then calls it. |
| `dispute_id` | The reference number of the resolved card dispute whose provisional credit is taken back, as returned by the card dispute lookup for the cardholder's account. Identifier text. |
| `reversal_usd` | The amount taken back, in US dollars, a positive number with 2 decimal places. A value with more decimals is rounded half up to the cent before it posts. |
| Return | A confirmation line naming the reversal's transaction reference number, the dispute reference number, the provisional credit it points to, the amount taken back in US dollars with two decimals and the card's new available balance in US dollars with two decimals. The transaction reference number shows the reversal posted. |
| Errors | Nothing posts in these cases: `reversal_usd` is not a positive dollar amount; there is no card dispute with that reference; the dispute is not a claim about a lost or stolen card; it is not resolved (with an error found or with no error); the card is not on the Advantage plan; or the dispute carries no provisional credit. |
